result.answer:
I've filled in the Kaiju-Proximity Construction Permit application form (found at **/permits/proximity/apply/**) with the following details, as requested, without submitting it:

| Field | Value entered |
|---|---|
| Applicant name | Mira Tanaka |
| Organisation | Tanaka Bakery |
| Contact email | mira@tanaka-bakery.example |
| Contact phone | 0299-55-0184 |
| Site postcode | 315-0117 |
| Evacuation zone | Zone 4 |
| Distance from corridor centreline | 300 m |
| Structure type | Structural alteration |
| Floor area | 96 m² |
| Reinforcement standard | K-2 (zone 4 minimum) — this is the correct minimum for Zone 4, per site rules |
| Seismic and impact mitigation plan attached | Yes |
| Planned start date | 2026-10-01 |

A few notes before you submit:

- **Reinforcement standard**: I selected K-2, since the site states Zone 4 requires at minimum K-2, and applications declaring a lower standard are refused outright with no refund. If your engineer's plan specifies a higher standard (K-3), you should update this field to match, since it must "meet or exceed" the zone minimum.
- **Documents**: The requirements page lists four required documents for a complete application — (1) site plan at 1:500 or finer showing the centreline, (2) the seismic/impact mitigation plan from your structural engineer, (3) a corridor proximity survey no older than 6 months, and (4) a copy of your contractor's prefecture licence. The form only has a checkbox/field for the mitigation plan — you may need to attach the other three documents separately, or there may be an upload step revealed after this form loads fully, so check the live page before submitting.
- **Fee**: ¥45,000 is payable on submission and is non-refundable if the application is refused.
- **Timing**: You're applying well ahead of the 1 October 2026 start date, which satisfies the "at least 10 business days before works begin" rule and leaves margin for the standard 10-business-day processing time (which only starts once the application is complete with all documents).

The form is ready for your review — I have not clicked Submit.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
